reports.title: Corinne Haslam: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: The court heard evidence as to the barriers which exist and make it difficult for staff working on mental health wards to obtain input from physical health specialists without sending a patient to hospital via the Emergency Department
concerns.hazard: lack of mental health ward access to physical health specialists

concerns.quote: It is a matter of concern that Mental Health Trusts and Acute Trusts operate different (apparently incompatible) electronic records systems
concerns.hazard: information silos between mental and physical health

concerns.quote: It is a matter of concern that ward-based nursing staff do not appear to have been provided with clear and unambiguous guidance as to the circumstances when a risk assessment for Venous Thromboembolism ('VTE') should be undertaken following admission to a ward, and the circumstances in which such risk assessment should be repeated
concerns.hazard: lack of VTE risk assessment guidance

links.explanation: Both reports concern deficiencies in venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk assessment linked to trust policy. The earlier report notes missing assessments despite existing policy, while the later report highlights confusion and weakening of the current VTE policy affecting assessments.
links.earlier_quote: At no time during the two periods of Ms [name redacted] inpatient care was she assessed for venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk in contravention of trust policy.
links.later_quote: During the course of Sophie's inquest, I heard evidence which concerns me that there is a lack of clarity in relation to the current local VTE policy.
links.promise_quote: A full review of the Trust's VTE policy

links.explanation: Both reports identify failures in ensuring proper venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk assessment for inpatients. The earlier report notes that no VTE assessment was performed, while the later report highlights absent clear guidance on when such assessments should be done or repeated.
links.earlier_quote: At no time during the two periods of Ms [name redacted] inpatient care was she assessed for venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk in contravention of trust policy.
links.later_quote: It is a matter of concern that ward-based nursing staff do not appear to have been provided with clear and unambiguous guidance as to the circumstances when a risk assessment for Venous Thromboembolism ('VTE') should be undertaken following admission to a ward, and the circumstances in which such risk assessment should be repeated.
links.promise_quote: A VTE Screening and Assessment Clinical Alert was disseminated across the Trust
